text:
maria: FYI seeing a surge of pod restarts in eastus2 gpupool, ~120 drops in last 15m, affected model-serving and prefetch pods
jevon: on it — is this the conntrack thing again or something new?
ash: symptoms look like SNAT/ephemeral port exhaustion, pods losing outbound conn and liveness probes fail
maria: flow: model pods -> node SNAT -> service host -> model backend in-cluster. After node kernel bump last night, we started hitting TCP TIME_WAIT retention higher than usual
kai: can someone paste `conntrack -S` and `ss -s`? I want to see table usage and TCP states
ash: grabbing now, output: 
```
# conntrack -S
entries: 262140
found: 12345678
searched: 9876543
insert: 120000
delete: 118000
```
`ss -s` shows high TIME-WAIT: tcp: 150k established, 90k time-wait
lucy: 262k conntrack entries is basically at kube node max (we set nf_conntrack_max=262144 on nodes for now)
maria: logs show repeated `connect: -71` and `i/o timeout` from prefetch sidecars then pod restarts due to failed readiness
jevon: are we seeing packet loss between pods (east-west)? latency spikes in calico?
ash: calico metrics show no large packet drop rates, but MTU mismatch warnings on a subset of nodes that had kernel upgrade (Mellanox RDMA enabled); some pods using hostNetwork avoided it
kai: RDMA and MTU mismatch could cause fragmentation and influence conntrack behavior if lots of retransmits. But the counts point to ports exhausted rather than pure packet loss
lucy: checking node kernel params, three nodes had nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait bumped to 600s during the update (should be 120s). That explains TIME-WAIT hangup and ephemeral port reuse delay
maria: ok that maps. Is fastest mitigation increase nf_conntrack_max or lower the TIME-WAIT?
ash: short-term: lower TIME-WAIT on those nodes to 120 and reboot kube-proxy to clear iptables SNAT entries. Also we can enable conntrack hashing tuning — but that’s medium effort
jevon: rolling change: patch daemonset that applied the kernel tuning? Which change pushed 600s? config-mgmt?
ash: it came from the kernel-ops patch baked into the image used by nodeup on last canary run — ops rolled it to a subset of eastus2 nodes
kai: plan: 1) run a 6-node rolling restart of affected nodes with corrected sysctl (nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=120) 2) bump nf_conntrack_max to 400k cluster-wide (temporary) 3) restart kube-proxy on each node after sysctl 4) watch conntrack entries and pod restarts
lucy: added a short-lived job to run `conntrack -D -p tcp --timeout 600` on the worst nodes to prune stale entries (only after traffic drops), to avoid collateral deletion
maria: also traffic shaping: move model-prefetch to nodes with hostNetwork and bypass SNAT for now to reduce ephemeral port use
ash: I'm kicking off node restarts now, starting with canary ring (3 nodes), will roll forward if stable
sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1287 — elevated pod restart rate eastus2 gpupool. Pager schedule: on-call SRE
deploy-bot: Rolling restart started: node-gpupool-eu-1 -> node-gpupool-eu-2 (canary)
jevon: monitoring: watch conntrack/entries, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, calico_tx_errors, and node_exporter netstat states
kai: if restarts don't bring connections down within 10m we'll route traffic to westus while we do deeper forensics
lucy: noting cost: bumping nf_conntrack_max to 400k increases memory footprint ~120MB per node — ops approved as short-term emergency tradeoff
maria: update: canary nodes restored sysctl and kube-proxy restarted, conntrack entries dropped from 260k -> 38k, pod restart rate back to baseline after 4m
ash: great — rolling to remaining nodes now
jevon: follow-ups: 1) revert the kernel-ops patch that changed TIME_WAIT default and make it explicit in node images 2) add conntrack saturation alert (80% of nf_conntrack_max) with playbook 3) consider SNAT avoidance for egress-heavy gpu workloads (hostNetwork or eBPF SNAT policy)
kai: also schedule RDMA/MTU audit on the cluster to avoid fragmented flows in the future
maria: thanks team. Filing postmortem next — will include timeline and mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
